speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand your condition, please describe the exact location, severity (on a scale of 1 to 10), and onset of your chest pain, and tell me if you have experienced any shortness of breath, sweating, or dizziness.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture)

The history of forceful vomiting after alcohol consumption followed by sudden chest pain and choking is highly characteristic of esophageal rupture. Given the severity and inability to communicate effectively, I am ordering a Water-Soluble Contrast Esophagram to confirm the diagnosis immediately.
